statement.p: The figure below open cylindrical can, S, standing on the xy-plane. (S has a bottom and sides, but no top.)
The side of S is given by x^2 + y^2 = 4, and its height is 4.
(a) Give a parametric equation, \vec r(t) for the rim, C.

p.em: (For this problem, enter your vector equation with angle-bracket notation: \lt f(t), g(t), h(t)>.)

statement.p: (b) If S is oriented outward and downward, find \int_S\mbox{curl }(-4 y\vec i+ 4 x\vec j+ z\vec k)\cdot d\vec A.

p.m: \int_S\mbox{curl }(-4 y\vec i+ 4 x\vec j+ z\vec k)\cdot d\vec A =

static.solution:
(a) The equation of the rim, C, is x^2+y^2=4, z=0. This is a circle of radius 2 centered on the z-axis, and lying in the plane z=2. We can parameterize this as \vec r(t) = 2\cos\mathopen{}\left(t\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}-2\sin\mathopen{}\left(t\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+4\,\mathit{\vec k},\quad 0\le t\le 2\pi.
(b) Use Stokes' Theorem, with C oriented clockwise when viewed from above: \int_S\mbox{curl }(-4 y\vec i+4 x\vec j+ z\vec k)\cdot d\vec A = \int_C(-4 y\vec i+ 4 x\vec j+ z\vec k)\cdot d\vec r. Since C is horizontal, the \vec k component does not contribute to the integral. The remaining vector field, -4 y\vec i+ 4 x\vec j, is tangent to C, of constant magnitude ||-4 y\vec i+4 x\vec j||= 8 on C, and points in the opposite direction to the orientation. Thus \int_S\mbox{curl }(-4 y\vec i+4 x\vec j+ z\vec k)\cdot d\vec A = \int_C(-4 y\vec i+ 4 x\vec j)\cdot d\vec r = -8\cdot \hbox{ Length of curve } = -8\cdot 2\pi 2 = -32\pi.
